observation.visible_scene: A low-angle, upward-looking view through a canopy of green oak leaves that frame the edges of the shot, with a bright pale-blue sky behind them. The sun shines directly toward the camera from near the center, producing a strong white glare and a faint circular lens-flare disc in the upper-central area. The leaves are backlit, with some appearing translucent and vivid green while others are darker silhouettes.
visible_changes: The oak leaves sway gently and continuously throughout the excerpt, with the central leaf cluster and the surrounding branches shifting slightly in position and orientation relative to the frame edges.

The bright core of the sun's glare moves in apparent position relative to the leaves: it is partly exposed in early frames and becomes more diffused and shifted toward the center-right in later frames, as leaves drift in front of and behind it.
The intensity of backlighting on individual leaves varies as their angles change during the sway, making some leaves flash brighter and others darken.
The faint lens-flare disc near the top center persists and drifts slightly along with the changing sun-leaf geometry.
The overall framing of the leaf border remains largely consistent, indicating the camera is mostly stationary while the apparent motion comes from the leaves and the shifting glare.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the breeze or any camera motion continues before t=0 or after t=3.2s.
The true position of the sun in the sky and the broader environment outside the leaf frame.
uncertain_details: It is unclear whether the slight apparent drift of the sun and flare is due purely to leaf movement, a small camera drift, or both; the background sky provides little evidence to separate them.
The apparent movement of the sun is an effect of occlusion and camera/leaf motion, not the sun itself moving.
